A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey. All 26 pages of v2 and 35 pages of v3 support comparison, including the tables, figures, and references. Neither contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v2 presents a literature survey and conceptual taxonomy. Its empirical findings are attributed to cited studies; no original experimental or data-analysis results are reported.

after.justification: v3 remains a survey. Tables 2–4 explicitly summarize results reported by other works, and the added CRE-Router discussion also cites a separate publication.

M1.justification: The survey retains its six routing paradigms and three-axis conceptual framework. Added and revised descriptions of cited algorithms do not establish a new or modified algorithm proposed by this work.

E1.justification: VL-RouterBench, RouterArena, DSC, and other evaluation efforts enter the literature review. Neither version actually uses datasets or tasks to conduct its own training or evaluation.

E2.justification: Tables 2–4 newly document comparator sets from cited studies. Neither version evaluates a proposed system against baselines, and these disclosures do not establish changes to the underlying studies' comparator membership.

E3.justification: v3 adds descriptions of AIQ, APGR, CPT, and published evaluation settings. These document existing practices rather than introduce or revise an evaluation protocol executed by the survey.

E4.justification: Sections 9.1 and 9.4 add literature-based discussion of attacks, distribution shift, and routing failures. They do not introduce an independently conducted ablation, robustness experiment, or empirical error analysis; the additions concern synthesis and interpretation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports original repeated-run estimates, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The expanded discussion of model confidence concerns routing signals rather than statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 add extensive quantitative evidence from cited studies, including Cascade Routing's 87.24% versus 84.48% AUC. MixLLM's 97.25% quality at 24.18% cost is retained through relocation, while R2-Reasoner's 84.46% cost-saving figure is removed. These are changes in reported literature results, not demonstrated performance improvements between versions.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal proofs or derivations. v3 adds informal summaries of cited regret guarantees and metric concepts, without presenting new formal statements or mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The taxonomy, conceptual framework, and central claim about model complementarity remain intact. The abstract and conclusion add emphasis on evaluation, particularly the need for standardized protocols across routing methods.

C2.justification: New Sections 9.3–9.4 explain why shared benchmarks do not ensure comparable results and analyze distribution shift, router staleness, asymmetric errors, and routing collapse. Section 12 adds substantive discussion of population disparities, feedback bias, provider–user incentive conflicts, and resource overhead.

D1.justification: Tables 2–4 newly disclose selected settings from cited experiments, including MixLLM's 80/20 split and UniRoute's 50/50 model split. Sections 6.1 and 7 also revise technical descriptions of Confidence-Driven Router supervision and FrugalGPT's offline-learned model order and thresholds.

R1.justification: The literature coverage expands substantially, adding approaches such as RouterDC, HAPS, CRE-Router, adapter routing, causal routing, and personalized routing. New work on adversarial robustness, evaluation deficiencies, and user incentives broadens the survey's research positioning beyond efficiency-oriented method summaries.

P1.justification: The existing section sequence and much of the prose are retained. v3 rewrites selected method descriptions, renames Section 6.2, adds evaluation subsections and an ethical statement, and strengthens cross-references to the conceptual framework.

P2.justification: v3 adds three substantial tables combining published results, baselines, and settings. Table 1 gains CRE-Router, and the former Table 2 becomes Table 5 with revised entries and sizing. Figures 1–3 retain identical image content and move with the surrounding text.

improvement.justification: v2 largely inventories methods, benchmarks, and metrics. v3 substantially strengthens the survey through contextualized quantitative comparisons, explicit explanations of evaluation incompatibility, and detailed failure and ethical analyses. Its revised technical accounts also distinguish routing mechanisms from evaluation procedures more clearly. These additions materially improve the survey's usefulness and critical depth without relying on claims of new experimental performance.
